output.brief: Don't discipline drivers or retrain everyone. The evidence points to contaminated brake fluid. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans while our own brake bay was closed. Eleven of them used fluid from one old bulk drum that had lost its cap and absorbed water. Those same 11 vans are exactly the 11 that generated all 27 complaints. The two Northfield vans that got fluid from a fresh drum had no complaints. Two returned vans tested at a boiling point of about 150°C against 255°C for sealed stock, and the pedal softened on long hills. The same drivers had no problems in other vans on the same hilly routes. The new pads, the new routes and the reporting app don't explain this pattern. Northfield recommended rechecking the other vans on 25 Sep, but nobody replied. Action this week: pull the 11 bulk-drum vans, and ideally all 13 Northfield vans, test the fluid, renew it from sealed stock and return them to service. Keep LK-209 parked until it is done. Tell drivers that reporting is welcome. Also confirm that the in-house and Calder Road vans did not use contaminated fluid. Confidence is high. Pad noise is a separate, unresolved question. Don't switch suppliers on this evidence.
